attribution.note: Zitron's own analysis in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the joint antecedent (revenue of $4.5B and that much cash in the bank), the $2B minimum with $10B upper case, and the 12-month horizon. 'Will have to' is firm necessity, so this is a scored conditional forecast.

contract.note: A July 29, 2025 deadline, reading $2B as the floor, and separating need from actual fundraising are all fair. The contract correctly makes resolution depend on first establishing the hypothetical starting conditions.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure of a $6.6B raise inside the window. It shows money was raised, not that it was needed under the stated scenario, and it does not establish the starting cash or revenue.

reviews.rationale: The deadline has passed, but nothing in the packet establishes the antecedent: about $4.5B revenue and about $4.5B in cash as of July 2024. With the condition unknown, the forecast is not scored. The October 2024 raise shows fundraising happened, not that it was necessary under the scenario, so the evidence does not settle the outcome.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The market collapse given 'without OpenAI' is stated firmly. The stock effect is hedged ('more than likely'), so that part is not scored. The antecedent is kept and there is no horizon.

contract.note: Reading 'without OpenAI' as a lasting collapse or exit is ordinary and fair. Correctly holds that OpenAI continuing to operate does not contradict the conditional.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement, dated the evaluation date, shows it still operating. That is evidence about the condition, not the outcome, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, a world without OpenAI, has not happened: the company is still operating as of the evaluation date. So the conditional is not scored and there is no post-trigger market to assess. The stock component is hedged and would be not_adjudicable in any case.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. He cites Google's report as his source, but endorses the claim himself.

semantics.note: Keeps the global emissions claim, the Google 48% example, and the 'thanks to AI' attribution. Correctly classed as causal.

contract.note: Treating 2019–2023 as the five years and 'massively increasing global emissions' as a substantial worldwide effect is an ordinary reading. Requiring the global component as well as the Google number decides the result.

evidence.note: BBC reporting confirms Google's 2023 emissions were 48% above 2019, and that Google itself tied the rise to AI compute energy demand. Independent measurement of AI's share is absent.
Google's own disclosure attributes the 13% year-over-year rise to data center energy and supply chain. It does not quantify AI's share of the five-year increase.

reviews.rationale: The 48% Google figure is supported, and Google's own report links the rise partly to AI compute. That link is a company disclosure, not an independent measurement. Nothing in the packet establishes a massive worldwide emissions increase caused by AI, and nothing refutes it. Since the contract requires both components, the claim as a whole is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: Captures the factual core: the estimated $3.5–4.5B in 2024 revenue cannot sustain the company. The surrounding 'must grow' is normative framing, rightly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'not enough to keep this company going' as revenue failing to cover the estimated 2024 operating costs is the ordinary financial reading and is fair. It does not require insolvency.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report of The Information's analysis: estimated 2024 operating costs of about $8.5B against $3.5–4.5B revenue. It is a secondary summary of estimates.

reviews.rationale: Credible contemporaneous reporting estimated OpenAI's 2024 operating costs at about $8.5B, well above the full $3.5–4.5B revenue range. That meets the contract's support condition. The figures are estimates, not audited accounts, and the packet contains no counterevidence.
